NA-safe grouping keys

Source: R/utils-na-keys.R
key_has_na_mask.Rd

Internal helpers that stop rows with a missing identifier from being merged into one group. They are shared by dedupe(), summarize_duplicates(), classify_duplicates(), and link_encounters().

Usage

key_has_na_mask(data, cols)

na_safe_group_id(data, cols)

inform_na_key_rows(n_na_key, fac_col_str, visit_col_str, inform_fn)

Arguments

data

A data frame.

cols

Character vector of the key column names in data.

n_na_key

Integer. Number of rows with a missing key.

fac_col_str, visit_col_str

Names of the facility and visit columns, used in the message.

inform_fn

A function taking a single message string.

Value

key_has_na_mask() returns a logical vector, TRUE where any of cols is NA. na_safe_group_id() returns an integer group id per row. inform_na_key_rows() returns NULL invisibly.

Details

dplyr::group_by() and .by = follow SQL's GROUP BY convention, in which every NA is equal to every other NA for grouping purposes, even though NA == NA evaluates to NA everywhere else in R. For a facility_col x visit_col key a missing value means the row's true identity is unknown, not confirmed to match every other row with a missing value, so grouping NAs together silently merges genuinely distinct visits (several rows with no Visit_ID would collapse into one during dedupe(), or read as artificially "duplicated" in summarize_duplicates()/classify_duplicates()).

na_safe_group_id() groups rows with no NA in cols exactly as dplyr::group_by() would, and places every row with any NA in cols in a singleton group of its own. The group key joins the columns with the ASCII unit-separator control character (U+001F), which cannot occur in an ESSENCE identifier, so two different key pairs can never concatenate to the same string (for example facility 100 + visit "15" versus facility 1001 + visit "5").

inform_na_key_rows() emits the standard informational message when na_safe_group_id() exempted one or more rows. inform_fn is either rlang::inform (dedupe() and summarize_duplicates(), which have no verbose argument) or a closure over inform_if() (classify_duplicates() and link_encounters(), which do).
